Modified assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- The 25 bp cut and “balanced risks” language point to modest, forecast-based easing as inflation moves closer to, but above, 2 percent; continued QT and a hawkish dissent cap the dovish tone.
- SLOOS signals credit remains restrictive where it matters for growth: banks report tight C&I standards (especially for small firms) and ongoing tightening in CRE; demand is weaker for small and some middle‑market firms. These are headwinds that justify easing but also argue against an aggressive pivot.
- Offsets in SLOOS temper the dovish read-through: residential real estate and HELOC standards are broadly unchanged, large banks eased multifamily standards, and foreign banks report stronger C&I demand with unchanged standards. Subprime consumer standards remain tighter.
Net: still mildly dovish, but the mixed SLOOS details nudge the overall tone slightly closer to neutral than a statement-only read.
